latest_release.name: Release v26.0.0
latest_release.body:
## BoxMOT v26.0.0

BoxMOT v26.0.0 adds multimodal tracking, optional EdgeTAM mask guidance, typed tracker configuration, and joint motion-model selection. It also improves evaluation reproducibility, replay performance, and tuning diagnostics.

Based on committed changes since `v25.0.0`, through `9da023fd`.

### New features and improvements

- **EagerMOT sensor fusion:** Track objects using calibrated 2D and 3D detections, with optional camera poses. New spatial structures represent 3D boxes, camera calibration, and multimodal outputs. Includes KITTI evaluation, class-specific tuning, and 3D Kalman calibration.
- **MAF-HDA mask tracking:** Adds a Python tracker combining motion with mask-based correlation-filter appearance. Supports AABB detections with instance masks without requiring ReID weights.
- **EdgeTAM integration:** Generate detection masks with the standalone segmentor or enable temporal mask-guided association using `--edgetam`. Guidance supports the nine Python box trackers with AABB geometry, IoU association, and `per_class=False`.
- **Typed configuration and simpler factories:** All eleven trackers expose immutable, validated configuration classes with editor completion. Detector, ReID, and tracker factories support simpler construction, while shared `KalmanConfig` and `ReIDConfig` group component settings.
- **Joint motion selection:** `tune --select-kf` compares compatible Kalman filters and noise profiles using held-out predictions. Add `--select-cmc` to jointly select camera-motion compensation. Selected profiles are saved for reuse.
- **More targeted tuning:** Conditional search spaces account for geometry, association metric, and enabled features. New controls expose motion, detection-confidence, and ReID–IoU fusion, with improved trial comparisons and parameter diagnostics.
- **Expanded evaluation:** Adds KITTI-MOTS mask evaluation, saved 2D detection workflows, 3D tracking metrics, and optional official KITTI AP40 reports. Materialized AABB evaluation supports ordered GTA, GSI, and GBRC postprocessing while preserving raw results.
- **Faster repeated workloads:** Batched Kalman operations, optimized camera-motion compensation, indexed embedding reads, reusable workers, and optional `--cache-inputs` reduce repeated processing.
- **Reliability fixes:** Restores per-sequence evaluation reporting, corrects DeepOC-SORT covariance handling during camera compensation, cleans up orphaned workers, and fixes Python 3.10 typing compatibility. OpenCV is pinned to `4.11.0.86`, and its runtime version participates in perception-cache identity.

### Breaking changes

This major release includes breaking changes. When upgrading from v25:

- **Update direct tracker construction.** Pass algorithm settings through the matching config, such as `BotSort(config=BotSortConfig(...))`. The factory also accepts algorithm keywords: `create_tracker("botsort", match_thresh=0.8)`.
- **Group component settings.** Move flat Kalman options into `kalman` and `kalman.noise`; configure tracker-owned appearance through `reid=ReIDConfig(...)` or an injected appearance encoder.
- **Replace `track_buffer`.** ByteTrack and BoT-SORT now use `max_lost_frames`, counted directly in tracker updates without FPS scaling.
- **Review removed tracker features.** SAM2MOT has been removed; standalone SAM segmentation remains available. OccluBoost's online GTA controls are removed, and its AABB/OBB thresholds and lifetime settings are consolidated.
- **Review centroid thresholds.** `centroid_max_distance` now determines geometric eligibility across matching and recovery; overlap thresholds no longer restrict centroid matching.
- **Update commands and imports.** Replace `boxmot time-variant` with `boxmot materialize --time-variant`. Internal tracker and motion modules have moved; prefer public imports from `boxmot`.
- **Rebuild native libraries.** ByteTrack, BoT-SORT, and OccluBoost use constructor ABI v3. Their shared update/res

Pluggable Python and C++ multi-object tracking modules for axis-aligned and oriented bounding box detections from any model.

[![CI](https://github.com/mikel-brostrom/boxmot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mikel-brostrom/boxmot/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/mikel-brostrom/boxmot/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/mikel-brostrom/boxmot/tree/master) [![PyPI version](https://badge.fury.io/py/boxmot.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/py/boxmot) [![downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/badge/boxmot)](https://pepy.tech/project/boxmot) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL%203.0-blue)](https://github.com/mikel-brostrom/boxmot/blob/master/LICENSE) [![python-version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/boxmot)](https://badge.fury.io/py/boxmot) [![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.8132989.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8132989) [![colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/18nIqkBr68TkK8dHdarxTco6svHUJGggY?usp=sharing) [![discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1377565354326495283?logo=discord&label=discord&labelColor=fff&color=5865f2)](https://discord.gg/tUmFEcYU4q) [](https://deepwiki.com/mikel-brostrom/boxmot) --- [Docs](docs/index.md) • [Installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md) • [Modes](docs/modes/index.md) • [API Reference](docs/python/index.md) • [Trackers](docs/trackers/index.md) • [Datasets](docs/datasets/index.md) • [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
BoxMOT provides independent detector, segmentor, appearance-encoder, and tracker components built around validated Torch structures. Pipelines compose those components; the CLI owns sources, outputs, materialized datasets, evaluation, tuning, research, and ReID workflows. ## Why BoxMOT - One interface for `track`, `materialize`, `materialize --time-variant`, `eval`, `tune`, `research`, `train-reid`, `eval-reid`, `compare-reid`, `export`, `install`, and native `build` workflows. - Swappable components with explicit capabilities and requirements. - Immutable, keyed Parquet builds with reusable detections, masks, and embeddings. - Support for both AABB and OBB tracking paths. - Optional native C++ tracker implementations selected with `--tracker-backend cpp`, with shared detection/output contracts and documented backend differences. They are also embeddable in standalone C++ projects through CMake (see [Native C++ Integration](docs/native/index.md) and [platform dependency installation](docs/native/index.md#install-dependencies)). - A structured Python API for embedding components and pipelines in applications. ## Installation BoxMOT supports Python `3.10` through `3.13`. ```bash pip install boxmot "ultralytics>=8.4.58" boxmot --help ``` This installs BoxMOT and the Ultralytics detector backend used below. For tracking existing detections through the Python API, `pip install boxmot` is enough. See [Installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md) for optional workflows and [PyTorch and source setup](docs/getting-started/pytorch.md) for CPU/CUDA profiles and YOLOX. For CUDA materialization, measure and apply detector/ReID batch sizes with: ```bash boxmot materialize --experiment mot17/ablation-yolox-lmbn.yaml --device cuda:0 --auto-batch ``` See [automatic GPU batch sizing](docs/modes/materialize.md#automatic-gpu-batch-sizing) for supported backends, memory limits, and sizing one stage at a time. ## Benchmark Results

Related guides: - [Evaluation and Postprocessing](docs/guides/evaluation.md) - [Experiment Workflows](docs/guides/experiments.md) - [Native C++ Integration](docs/native/index.md) ## Minimal Usage The [mode guides](https://mikel-brostrom.github.io/boxmot/modes/) provide toggleable **CLI** and **Python** examples for tracking, materialization, evaluation, tuning, research, ReID training, and export. Python workflow functions accept settings directly as keyword arguments. Select a command, detector, ReID model, tracker, and other settings interactively: ```bash boxmot ui ``` The [terminal UI](docs/modes/ui.md) previews the command before you run it and enables an interactive dashboard for workflows that report live progress. To track objects you select yourself, choose `track` and tracker `edgetam` in the launcher. Its video window accepts bounding boxes or foreground/background points, then propagates object masks and IDs. See the [EdgeTAM setup and controls](docs/trackers/edgetam.md). To evaluate EdgeTAM by prompting each pedestrian at its first fully visible, in-frame ground-truth box, use `boxmot eval --dataset mot17-mini --tracker edgetam --prompt-source first-visible`. See the [prompted evaluation protocol](docs/trackers/edgetam.md#evaluate-first-visible-people) for visibility requirements, object capacity, and scoring. CLI: ```bash boxmot track --detector yolo26n --reid lmbn_n_duke --tracker occluboost \ --source 0 --save --show ``` Evaluate a tracker: ```bash boxmot eval \ --dataset mot17 \ --split ablation \ --detector yolox-x-mot17 \ --reid lmbn-n-duke \ --tracker botsort ``` Python trackers except SFSORT, plus native ByteTrack, BotSort, OcSort, and OccluBoost, support opt-in capture timing with `--variable-dt` or `KalmanConfig(variable_dt=True)`. The Python API requires a timestamp on every update. SFSORT uses fixed steps on both backends. See [elapsed-time tracking](https://mikel-brostrom.github.io/boxmot/python/#elapsed-time). Python with axis-aligned boxes (AABB): ```python import numpy as np from boxmot import OccluBoost tracker = OccluBoost() dets = np.array([[100, 200, 300, 400, 0.9, 0]]) frame = np.zeros((480, 640, 3), dtype=np.uint8) # BGR image tracks = tracker.update(dets, frame) print(tracks[:, 4].astype(int)) # track IDs ``` Python with oriented boxes (OBB): ```python import numpy as np from boxmot import OccluBoost tracker = OccluBoost(is_obb=True) # cx, cy, width, height, angle in radians, confidence, class_id dets = np.array([[200, 300, 200, 100, np.pi / 6, 0.9, 0]]) frame = np.zeros((480, 640, 3), dtype=np.uint8) # BGR image tracks = tracker.update(dets, frame) print(tracks[:, 5].astype(int)) # track IDs ``` 2D/3D sensor fusion with ego-motion compensation using [EagerMot](docs/trackers/eagermot.md): ```python import numpy as np import torch from boxmot import EagerMot from boxmot.structures import CameraModel tracker = EagerMot() projection = torch.tensor([ # synthetic camera projection [100, 0, 100, 0], [0, 100, 50, 0], [0, 0, 1, 0], ], dtype=torch.float32) camera_to_world = torch.eye(4, dtype=torch.float32) camera_to_world[0, 3] = 1.0 # synthetic pose: camera at world x = 1 meter camera = CameraModel( projection=projection, image_size=(100, 200), # height, width camera_to_world=camera_to_world, ) dets = np.array([[78, 39, 122, 62, 0.95, 0]]) # 3D in camera coordinates: x, y, z, yaw, length, width, height, confidence, class_id dets_3d = np.array([[0, 1, 10, 0, 4, 2, 2, 0.9, 0]]) tracks_2d, tracks_3d = tracker.update( dets, detections_3d=dets_3d, camera=camera, ) print(tracks_2d[:, 4].astype(int)) # image track IDs print(tracks_3d[:, 7].astype(int)) # 3D track IDs ``` Replace the synthetic pose with the current frame's absolute 4×4 camera-to-world transform on every update. KITTI evaluation loads these from `poses.npy` when the dataset declares a `poses` modality. If poses are unavailable, omit `CameraModel.camera_to_world` throughout the sequence to track in camera coordinates. A NumPy camera projection can also be passed with a frame that provides its image dimensions; use `CameraModel` when no frame is supplied. ## License BoxMOT is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3 (AGPL-3.0)](LICENSE). Each detector and segmentor integrated with BoxMOT retains its own upstream license. See the respective project's license for its terms. Other third-party components also retain their respective licenses and notices. ## Contributing Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [contributor docs](docs/contributing/index.md). ## Contributors ## Support and Citation - Bugs and feature requests: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/mikel-brostrom/boxmot/issues) - Questions and discussion: [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/mikel-brostrom/boxmot/discussions) or [Discord](https://discord.gg/tUmFEcYU4q) - Limited free consulting is available for nonprofit nature conservation projects using BoxMOT.
